lessons.title: A busy week
lessons.desc: Sáng Chủ nhật, Mike gặp Emma, cô hàng xóm, lúc đi dạo.

s.t: Morning, Mike! You look tired.
Is everything okay?

s.m: To be **hon**est, ↗ / I've been {**slammed**|be slammed} at work all **week**. ↘
s.t: To be honest, I've been slammed at work all week.
I hardly ever get home before eight.
Oh no.
Is the commute still that bad?
It's terrible.

s.m: The roads are so {con**gest**ed|congested}, ↗ / I got {**stuck**|stuck} in a {**traf**fic jam|traffic jam} for an **hour** yesterday. ↘
s.t: The roads are so congested, I got stuck in a traffic jam for an hour yesterday.

s.m: {That's **why**|That’s why} I {**go** for a **walk**|Go for a walk} every **morn**ing. ↘
s.t: That's why I go for a walk every morning.

s.m: It helps me {deal with **stress**|Deal with stress}. ↘
s.t: It helps me deal with stress.
I should do that, too.

s.m: But I never have any {**spare** time|Spare time}. ↘
s.t: But I never have any spare time.
You don't need a lot.
Just fifteen minutes a day.

s.m: It's {the **eas**iest thing|The easiest thing} you can do / for your {**men**tal **health**|mental health}. ↘
s.t: It's the easiest thing you can do for your mental health.
Fifteen minutes?
Okay, I guess I can try that.

s.m: And try to {get some **rest**|Get some rest} on the **week**ends. ↘
s.t: And try to get some rest on the weekends.
No laptop, no emails.
That's the hard part.

s.m: I {feel **stressed**|Feel stressed} / when I'm not **check**ing my **phone**. ↘
s.t: I feel stressed when I'm not checking my phone.
I know the feeling.

s.m: But you have to {**break** that **hab**it|Break a habit}. ↘
s.t: But you have to break that habit.
You're right.

s.m: So, ↗ / what's your {**main hob**by|Main hobby} these days? ↘
s.t: So, what's your main hobby these days?
Rollerblading!
There's a park near the river.

s.m: {Do you want to come a**long**?|Do you want to come along?} ↗
s.t: Do you want to come along?
I'd love to.

s.m: But I haven't done it in **years**. ↘
s.t: But I haven't done it in years.
I don't want to get hurt.
Don't be scared!
I'll teach you.
You'll make progress fast.
Okay, deal.

s.m: And {after **that**|And then / after that}, ↗ / I'll {**brew** a **cof**fee|Brew a coffee} for us, ↗ / with {**con**densed **milk**|Condensed milk}. ↘
s.t: And after that, I'll brew a coffee for us, with condensed milk.
Vietnamese coffee?
Definitely!
See you on Saturday!

lessons.title: Factory visit
lessons.desc: Sarah, người mua hàng của một hãng snack Mỹ, đến thăm nhà máy và bàn đơn túi mới với Mike, trưởng phòng kế hoạch.

s.t: Hi, Mike! Thanks for having me.

s.m: {To be **hon**est|To be Honest}, ↗ / I was a **lit**tle {**jet** lagged|jet lagged} this **morn**ing… ↗ / but {I'm **all** set‿now|you are all set}. ↘
s.t: To be honest, I was a little jet lagged this morning… but I'm all set now.
Welcome to our plant!

s.m: {Take your **time**|Take your time}. ↘ / Would you **like** some **cof**fee / before we **start**? ↗
s.t: Take your time. Would you like some coffee before we start?

s.m: We have {**ground** coffee|ground coffee}, ↗ / or {coffee sa**chets**|Coffee sachets}. ↘
s.t: We have ground coffee, or coffee sachets.
Oh, I'd love to.

s.m: So, ↗ / let me get {**straight**|Straight} to the **point**. ↘
s.t: So, let me get straight to the point.

s.m: Our **new** snack bag / has to be on the **shelves** / in **March**. ↘
s.t: Our new snack bag has to be on the shelves in March.
Can you meet that deadline?
I think so.
But it depends on the artwork.

s.m: Once you {ap**prove**|approve} the **fi**nal {**proof**|proofing / proof print}, ↗ / we can start {en**grav**ing the **cyl**inders|engraved cylinder} / right a**way**. ↘
s.t: Once you approve the final proof, we can start engraving the cylinders right away.

s.m: Okay. ↘ / And what's the {**lead** time|lead time}, / **rough**ly? ↘
s.t: Okay. And what's the lead time, roughly?
About three weeks.

s.m: **One** week for the **cyl**inders, ↗ / and **two** weeks for **print**ing, ↗ / **lam**inating, ↗ / and **mak**ing the **bags**. ↘
s.t: One week for the cylinders, and two weeks for printing, laminating, and making the bags.

s.m: {That's **why**|That’s why} / we need the artwork {in ad**vance**|in advance}. ↘
s.t: That's why we need the artwork in advance.
That makes sense.
And what about color?

s.m: **Last** year, / our **old** {sup**pli**er|supplier} had a **prob**lem with {**mis**register|misregister}… ↗ / and the **col**ors were {**slight**ly|Slightly} **off**. ↘
s.t: Last year, our old supplier had a problem with misregister… and the colors were slightly off.
I understand your concern.

s.m: Our **press**es have {auto **reg**ister con**trol**|auto register control}, ↗ / and we **check** every **roll** / with a {**line** scan **cam**era|camera / line scan camera}. ↘
s.t: Our presses have auto register control, and we check every roll with a line scan camera.

s.m: So, / de**fects** are **much** easier to {**catch**|Catch / Caught / caught}. ↘
s.t: So, defects are much easier to catch.
Good. And color matching?
We measure every color with a spectrophotometer.

s.m: If the {**Del**ta **E**|Delta E (ΔE)} is too **high**, ↗ / we ad**just** the {**ink** formula|ink formula / recipe} / be**fore** we **run**. ↘
s.t: If the Delta E is too high, we adjust the ink formula before we run.
Great. But not only that.

s.m: We **al**so ex**port** to **Eu**rope, ↗ / so we need {**low** migration **ink**|low migration ink}, ↗ / and **full** {tracea**bil**ity|traceability}. ↘
s.t: We also export to Europe, so we need low migration ink, and full traceability.
No problem.

s.m: **Ev**ery roll has a **code**, ↗ / so you can **trace** it **back** / to the e**xact** {**shift**|shift}. ↘
s.t: Every roll has a code, so you can trace it back to the exact shift.
Honestly, I was a bit nervous about changing suppliers.

s.m: But **some**times, / you **have** to {take a **risk**|Take a risk}. ↘
s.t: But sometimes, you have to take a risk.

s.m: {**Don't** be a**fraid**|Don't be afraid} / to {**ask** **ques**tions|Ask a question}. ↘
s.t: Don't be afraid to ask questions.

s.m: If **some**thing goes **wrong**, ↗ / we'll {take re**spon**si**bil**ity|Take responsibility}, ↗ / and we'll {**solve** the **prob**lem|Solve a problem} **fast**. ↘
s.t: If something goes wrong, we'll take responsibility, and we'll solve the problem fast.

s.m: **Then** I'd like a {**tri**al run|trial run / test run} **first**. ↘
s.t: Then I'd like a trial run first.

s.m: Could you **send** me a {quo**ta**tion|quotation / quote}, ↗ / {a**long** with|along with} a **few** **proof** prints? ↗
s.t: Could you send me a quotation, along with a few proof prints?
Sure.

s.m: I'll {re**ply** to your e**mail**|Reply to an email} by **Fri**day, ↗ / and I'll {con**firm**|confirm} the {**sched**ule|schedule} / after {the **morn**ing **brief**ing|The morning briefing} to**mor**row. ↘
s.t: I'll reply to your email by Friday, and I'll confirm the schedule after the morning briefing tomorrow.

s.m: **Per**fect. ↘ / I think we've {**come** to an a**gree**ment|Come to an agreement}. ↘
s.t: Perfect. I think we've come to an agreement.
Let's keep in touch!
Definitely. Thanks for coming, Sarah.
Enjoy the rest of your trip!

lessons.title: Hotel check-in
lessons.desc: Mike sang Chicago dự hội chợ bao bì, đến khách sạn lúc tối và nhận phòng với Anna ở quầy lễ tân.

s.t: Good evening, sir.
Welcome to the Lakeside Hotel.
Do you have a reservation?
Yes. It's under Mike Tran.
Sorry, I'm a little slow.
I just had a twelve-hour layover in Seoul.

s.m: Oh, ↗ / you must be {**jet** lagged|jet lagged}. ↘
s.t: Oh, you must be jet lagged.
How was the flight?
Long.

s.m: I had a **mid**dle {**seat**|seat}, ↗ / far from {the **aisle**|the aisle}. ↘
s.t: I had a middle seat, far from the aisle.
And the landing was a bit bumpy.
That sounds tiring.
Okay, I found your booking.
Three nights, non-smoking.
Perfect.

s.m: Is there a {**shut**tle|shuttle} / to the con**ven**tion center? ↗
s.t: Is there a shuttle to the convention center?
I'm here for a packaging trade show.
Yes.

s.m: The shuttle **leaves** every **thir**ty minutes, ↗ / from **sev**en in the **morn**ing. ↘
s.t: The shuttle leaves every thirty minutes, from seven in the morning.
Great.

s.m: Oh, ↗ / and I forgot my {**charg**er|A charger}. ↘
s.t: Oh, and I forgot my charger.

s.m: Do you have one / I could {**bor**row|borrow}? ↗
s.t: Do you have one I could borrow?
Of course.

s.m: I'll have someone {**fetch**|fetch} one for you. ↘
s.t: I'll have someone fetch one for you.

s.m: You can find all the other {a**men**ities|Amenity} / in the **room**. ↘
s.t: You can find all the other amenities in the room.
Thanks.

s.m: And can I **skip** the {**tow**el change|towel change}? ↗
s.t: And can I skip the towel change?
I'd like to save water.
Sure.
Just hang the sign on the door.

s.m: By the **way**, ↗ / it's going to **rain** tomorrow. ↘
s.t: By the way, it's going to rain tomorrow.

s.m: You might want to {**check** the **fore**cast|Check the forecast}. ↘
s.t: You might want to check the forecast.
Good to know.

s.m: My {i**tin**erary|Itinerary} is **pret**ty **full**, ↗ / but I'd **love** to {**wan**der|wander} around the **ci**ty on **Sun**day. ↘
s.t: My itinerary is pretty full, but I'd love to wander around the city on Sunday.
Then you should visit the Riverwalk.

s.m: And our {**roof**top|Rooftop} **bar** / has a **great** view of the {**sky**scrapers|skyscraper}. ↘
s.t: And our rooftop bar has a great view of the skyscrapers.
Sounds amazing.
One more thing.

s.m: I'd like to book a **tax**i to the **air**port {in ad**vance**|in advance}, ↗ / for **Wednes**day **morn**ing. ↘
s.t: I'd like to book a taxi to the airport in advance, for Wednesday morning.
No problem, I'll book it for you.
Here's your key.

s.m: Your room is **eight** twenty-**two**, ↗ / on the **eighth** floor. ↘
s.t: Your room is eight twenty-two, on the eighth floor.
Thank you so much, Anna.
You've been really helpful.
My pleasure.

s.m: En**joy** your **stay**, ↗ / and {get some **rest**|Get some rest}! ↘
s.t: Enjoy your stay, and get some rest!

lessons.title: A bowl of pho
lessons.desc: Sáng hôm sau buổi thăm nhà máy, Mike dẫn Sarah đi ăn phở ở Sài Gòn.

s.m: So, ↗ / this is my **fa**vorite **pho** place / in **Sai**gon. ↘
s.t: So, this is my favorite pho place in Saigon.
Have you tried Vietnamese cuisine before?

s.m: Only {**rice** wraps|rice wraps}, ↗ / back in Chi**ca**go. ↘
s.t: Only rice wraps, back in Chicago.
Nothing like this.
It smells amazing!
That's the broth.

s.m: They {**sim**mer|simmer} beef bones for **ten** hours, ↗ / with {**star** anise|star anise}, ↗ / {**cin**namon|Cinnamon}, ↗ / {**gin**ger|ginger}, ↗ / and {**charred**|charred} {**on**ion|onion}. ↘
s.t: They simmer beef bones for ten hours, with star anise, cinnamon, ginger, and charred onion.
Ten hours?
Wow.
So, what should I order?
The special.

s.m: It has **ev**erything: ↗ / thin {**slic**es|Slice} of **beef**, ↗ / **meat**balls, ↗ / and {**rice** noodles|rice noodles}. ↘
s.t: It has everything: thin slices of beef, meatballs, and rice noodles.

s.m: Okay, ↗ / {I'll **go** with|I'll go with} the **spe**cial, ↗ / and an {**iced tea**|iced tea}, please. ↘
s.t: Okay, I'll go with the special, and an iced tea, please.
Good choice.

s.m: Now, ↗ / add some {**herbs**|herbs}: ↗ / {**ba**sil|Basil}, ↗ / {**bean** sprouts|bean sprouts}, ↗ / and a little **lime**. ↘
s.t: Now, add some herbs: basil, bean sprouts, and a little lime.
What about this one?
The green leaves.
That's cilantro.

s.m: Some people **hate** it, ↗ / so {**take** a **bite**|take a bite} **first**. ↘
s.t: Some people hate it, so take a bite first.
Mmm… it's fine.
And these dipping sauces?
The brown one is hoisin, it's sweet.
The red one is chili.
It's really spicy.
I'll be careful.

s.m: Let me {**take** a **sip**|take a sip} of the broth **first**. ↘
s.t: Let me take a sip of the broth first.
Oh, it's rich, but light at the same time.
Exactly.
Southern pho is a bit sweeter.

s.m: In the **north**, ↗ / the broth is {**mild**er|milder}, ↗ / and they don't use as **ma**ny herbs. ↘
s.t: In the north, the broth is milder, and they don't use as many herbs.

s.m: {**Which** one do you pre**fer**?|Which one do you prefer?} ↘
s.t: Which one do you prefer?

s.m: I grew up in the **south**, ↗ / so {I'd **say**|I would say} **this** one. ↘
s.t: I grew up in the south, so I'd say this one.
I can see why.

s.m: It's **so** much better than {**West**ern food|Western food} / for **break**fast. ↘
s.t: It's so much better than Western food for breakfast.
Careful.

s.m: If you **fin**ish the **whole** bowl, ↗ / you'll get a {**food** coma|Food coma}. ↘
s.t: If you finish the whole bowl, you'll get a food coma.
Worth it!
Let's do this again tomorrow.
